author: t.wambsgans
content: I created a reproducible benchmark, where 4 cores are pinned to do the 16->1 recursive aggregation, and 4 cores execute the EVM (>80% busy, with disk IO). To run it: go inside the [leanVM](https://github.com/leanEthereum/leanVM) repo and run: `git fetch --all && git checkout bench-alongside-execution-client && bench/bench-alongside-el.sh`. On my Hetzner EX63 server, the performance is only <5% slower with the EL running alongside (2.1s vs 2.2s). But it's a server, it will likely be slower on a laptop due to the power being a bottleneck. I will try to run it on other machines and keep you updated.

author: t.wambsgans
content: Thanks to Kev I have now access to a machine with the same CPU as Potuz (`Intel Core Ultra 7 155H`) with a slightly worse RAM (`Crucial 16GB DDR5-5600 SODIMM`). **On 4 cores running the EL + 4 cores running the 16 -> 1 recursion, it takes 4.48 s**. (To be clear I voluntarily do not use all the cores of the machine, to be compliant with EIP-7870). I will try to see if we can get optimisations for this machine (I suspect yes).
